We need to add a new component to the run button on the card popups when an action is running on the card that has a task list.

With task lists, we can show a progress bar to show how far along the agent already is. A task list, is a list, it has multiple items, so we can turn that into a progress bar.

Use a horizontal progress bar, just below the run button.

We need to be careful when loading the component, it doesn't need to be there on every run button, only those that are currently running an action.

The component should be stand alone, so it monitors the changes, it is not provided with the progress value, but with the info needed to identify task list to track.

id: F_381
title: check for Codex CLI updates at startup
status: new
internalId: 567ff5d6-ed2a-4bad-85bc-902c21642604
after: 630757d3-c37f-4fa9-99f8-7b2fa20fbf97
---

At startup, check asynchronously whether the Codex CLI used by MDÂ² has a newer version available. When it can be updated, show the existing **Update Codex** snackbar action and use the existing update command.

## Current state

- [F_178](../releases/0_3_0/F_178_handle_codex_version_errors_better.md) added an update warning only after a Codex run reports a model-cache error and the running CLI version differs from the cache version. A newer published release alone produces no warning.
- `CodexCliUpdateService.start()` subscribes to that mismatch event during renderer startup. Its snackbar action calls the dedicated Electron `updateCodexCli()` bridge method, which runs `npm install --global @openai/codex@latest`.
- Codex commands come from agent profiles, so a configured executable may differ from the global npm installation that this command updates.

## Required behavior

- Start one background check when the desktop app starts, after the renderer subscribes to Codex update notifications. Do not delay startup, project loading, or agent use while checking. Browser mode has no check.
- In Electron, determine the version of the Codex executable that MDÂ² would run and the latest available version of `@openai/codex`. Compare versions numerically, including prerelease semantics; offer an update only when the published version is newer.
- Offer the existing npm update action only when the executable being checked is the global npm Codex installation that the action will update. If the executable is missing, its version cannot be read, the latest version cannot be obtained, or its installation source cannot be confirmed, do not claim that an update is available.
- Reuse the existing `CodexCliUpdateService` snackbar and `updateCodexCli()` bridge action. Refactor the warning payload and presentation as needed so a release update says **installed version â†’ available version**, while a model-cache mismatch keeps its distinct explanation. Deduplicate warnings if both checks identify the same needed update.
- Keep the existing model-cache diagnostic and its update warning. A failed startup check must not prevent that path from working. Keep the update button's current pending, success, failure, and retry behavior.

## Implementation and verification

- Add a bounded, asynchronous version query in the Electron Codex update path and expose only the resulting update status through the dedicated bridge. Keep command execution out of the renderer.
- Extend renderer startup to trigger the check after the update subscription is active. Keep the result in the existing update service rather than component state.
- Test newer, equal, older, and prerelease versions; missing or unconfirmed npm installation; unavailable version source; startup remaining usable while the check runs; and deduplication with the cache-mismatch warning. Verify that both warning sources invoke the same fixed update command.

[4456 characters omitted]
ime, the desktop `commit` in `project_files.js` stages that path as it is on disk and commits it together with the rest of the batch. A path that no longer exists is skipped.
* Every `CommitBatcher` flush reaches the desktop through the `commit` handler in `desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js`, which calls `localGitService.commit(request, currentLocalProject)` and ends in `commitNow` in `desktop/src/project/project_files.js`. `commitNow` writes and stages `files` and `moves`, stages each entry of `paths` as it is on disk (a missing path is skipped), and then calls `commitStagedChanges`. `commitStagedChanges` does nothing when nothing is staged.

## Implementation details

Goal: `usage_metrics.csv` never gets a commit of its own. It is added to commits that already happen. Each time the desktop commits a `CommitBatcher` flush for the active primary project, it also stages the usage metrics file. If the file is unchanged, `git add` stages nothing and the commit contains only the batch.

### Desktop

* `UsageMetricsService`: add `repositoryPath(rootPath)`. It returns the CSV path relative to the repository root, with forward slashes (for example `design/usage_metrics.csv`). It returns `null` when no project is active or when `rootPath` is not the bound project root (compare with `projectKey` from `project_operation_coordinator`). The absolute path is already stored in `this.filePath` by `startProject`.
* `local_bridge_dispatch.js`, `commit` handler: before calling `localGitService.commit`, add `usageMetricsService.repositoryPath(currentLocalProject.rootPath)` to `request.paths` when it is not `null`. Build the new request as one object, for example `{ ...request, paths: [...(request.paths ?? []), usageMetricsPath] }`. The commit message is not changed.
* `desktop/main.js`: pass `usageMetricsService` into `createLocalBridgeDispatch`.
* Keep `uncommittedProjectWrites.mark(...)` in `appendRecords`. When no batcher commit happens before the next worktree integration, the integration still commits the file. When a batch already committed it, `commitTrackedPaths` finds no staged changes and does nothing.
* No change in the app, in `CommitBatcher`, or in the direct activity commits (`commitTrackedPaths` in `project_agent_token_usage.js` and `activity_files.js`).

### Edge cases and side effects

* No usage metrics commits while nothing else is committed: rows written by the 2-minute account usage poll wait for the next batch commit or integration.
* An append that runs while a commit is staging: `appendRecords` runs inside `projectOperationCoordinator.run(rootPath, ...)` and `commit` runs inside `holdProjectMutation`, which uses the same coordinator. They cannot overlap, so a commit contains only complete rows.
* The file does not exist yet: `commitNow` skips the missing path.
* Worktree commits (`commitWorktree`) and integration are separate handlers and are not changed. The usage metrics file only lives in the primary worktree.
* Remote-control clients flush through the same desktop `commit` handler, so their commits also carry the file.

### Tests

* `desktop/src/actions/agent/usage_metrics_service.test.mjs`: `repositoryPath` returns the relative path for the bound root, and `null` for another root or before `startProject`.
* `desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.test.mjs`: `commit` adds the usage metrics path to `request.paths` next to existing paths, and leaves the request unchanged when `repositoryPath` returns `null`.

## Acceptance criteria

* `usage_metrics.csv` is never committed on its own: no new commit is created just because rows were appended.
* When the commit batcher commits other changes of the primary project, pending `usage_metrics.csv` changes are part of that same commit, with the batch's commit message.
* A batch commit while `usage_metrics.csv` is unchanged contains only the batch files.
* The next worktree integration still commits the file if no batch commit happened before it.
* The CSV content and format do not change.
* The new desktop tests pass, and lint passes in `desktop`.

Part of [F_380](F_380_add_possibility_to_support_task_tracking_tool.md). Show `conversation.taskList` from [F_431](F_431_agent_task_list_model_and_run_update.md) in the conversation chat.

## Current state

* `ActionConversationChat` (`app/src/components/actions/conversation/action_conversation_chat.tsx`) lays out the transcript, status area and prompt.
* Live conversations come from the run store in `action_run_registry.ts`; historical ones from `ActionConversationStore` (`resolveDisplayedConversation`).

## Implementation details

* New self-contained component `AgentTaskList` in `app/src/components/actions/conversation/tasks/agent_task_list.tsx`. It receives only what identifies the displayed conversation and subscribes itself with `useSyncExternalStore`; `getSnapshot` returns `conversation.taskList` (a stable reference that changes only on `agentTaskList`). No task data or handlers come from the parent, so it can be moved elsewhere later.
* Initial placement: in `ActionConversationChat`, directly above the prompt.
* Renders nothing when there is no list or it is empty.
* Each row: status icon (pending / in progress / completed) and text; an in-progress task shows `activeForm` when present, otherwise `subject`. Header shows `completed/total`. Collapsible, expanded by default, compact height with scrolling for long lists.
* Styling per `design/STYLE_GUIDE.md` and the existing conversation status components.
* Works the same for live and historical conversations.

## Tests

React Testing Library:

* Renders tasks with their states and the progress count.
* Shows `activeForm` for the in-progress task.
* Renders nothing without a task list.
* Updates when an `agentTaskList` update arrives.

Part of [F_380](F_380_add_possibility_to_support_task_tracking_tool.md). Provider-neutral task list on the conversation, persisted and sent to the renderer. Provider decoders ([F_432](F_432_claude_task_list_decoder.md), [F_433](F_433_codex_plan_decoder.md)) and the panel ([F_434](F_434_agent_task_list_component.md)) build on this.

## Current state

* Provider events become conversation entries in `agent_runner_service.js` (`handleProviderEvent`, `recordProviderEvent`) and reach the renderer as `agentEvent` updates with an `entryIndex` (`desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js`).
* Conversation-level fields use their own update kind, e.g. `agentUsage` (`action_run.js`, `app/src/data/action_run_types.ts`, `app/src/services/actions/action_run_registry.ts`).
* `parseAgentConversationValue` (`shared/agent_conversations.mjs`) rebuilds the conversation from known fields only, so an unknown field is lost on reload.

## Implementation details

* Shape, stored as `conversation.taskList`:

  ```
  { tasks: [{ id, subject, status: 'pending' | 'inProgress' | 'completed', activeForm? }], updatedAt }
  ```

  Every change replaces the whole list (Codex sends full snapshots; Claude lists are small).
* Desktop runner: a run event `{ type: 'taskList', taskList }` from either decoder sets `run.conversation.taskList`, is included in the persisted checkpoint, and is emitted to the action run.
* `action_run.js`: publish it as update `{ kind: 'agentTaskList', taskList }`, next to `agentUsage`. No new IPC channel.
* `shared/agent_conversations.mjs`: validate and keep `taskList` in `parseAgentConversationValue`. An invalid list fails the parse like other invalid fields. Conversations without the field have no `taskList`.
* Renderer types: add `taskList?` to `AgentConversation` (`app/src/data/data_types.ts`) and the update kind to `action_run_types.ts`.
* `action_run_registry.ts`: apply `agentTaskList` to `conversation.taskList` with its own `conversationChange` kind, so transcript subscribers do not treat it as an entry change.

## Tests

* `parseAgentConversationValue`: valid list kept, invalid list rejected, absent list stays absent.
* Runner/action run: a `taskList` run event updates the conversation and publishes `agentTaskList`.
* Registry: `agentTaskList` replaces `conversation.taskList` and leaves entries untouched.

+The component should be stand alone, so it monitors the changes, it is not provided with the progress value, but with the info needed to identify task list to track.
+
+## Current state
+
+* `CardRunButton` (`app/src/components/actions/run/trigger/card_run_button.tsx`) is rendered in each board card by `project_card_view.tsx`. It subscribes to the card context's first active run through `useRunningActionForContext`; that summary contains `runId` and status, but no task-list data.
+* A live task list is stored at `ActionRun.conversation.taskList`. Each `agentTaskList` update replaces that list in `ActionRunRegistry`, and `useRunSelector(runId, selector)` provides a run-scoped subscription.
+* `AgentTaskList` (`app/src/components/actions/conversation/tasks/agent_task_list.tsx`) already shows the same model in the action popup and defines progress as completed tasks divided by all tasks. Board cards currently show only the animated running border around the Run button.
+
+## Implementation details
+
+* Add a standalone `TaskProgressIndicator` component beside `CardRunButton`. It receives only `runId`, selects `run.conversation.taskList` with `useRunSelector`, and computes `completed / total` itself. Do not pass task data or a computed percentage from the parent.
+* Render a determinate MUI `LinearProgress` directly below the Run button. Give it an accessible label containing the completed and total counts, and style it only with theme values from `design/STYLE_GUIDE.md`.
+* Return `null` when the selected run has no task list or an empty task list. Task additions, removals, and status changes update the bar through the run-store subscription.
+* In `CardRunButton`, mount the indicator only when the live run status is exactly `running`, passing `runningRun.runId`. Do not show it for queued, waiting-for-input, idle, or terminal state. Keep current button state priority, tooltip, click behavior, and scheduled indicator unchanged.
+* Wrap the button and indicator in a compact vertical layout so the bar sits below the button without changing other footer controls. No task model, action protocol, persistence, registry, or desktop changes are needed.
+* Add focused React Testing Library coverage for the new component and its `CardRunButton` integration. Run affected tests and `npm run lint` in `app`.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+* While a card action has status `running` and a non-empty task list, a horizontal progress bar appears directly below that card's Run button.
+* Progress equals completed task count divided by total task count; pending and in-progress tasks are not counted as completed.
+* Bar updates when the active run publishes a replacement task list, without reopening the card or action popup.
+* No bar appears for a missing or empty task list, or while run is queued, waiting for input, idle, or finished.
+* Concurrent cards read their own active run by `runId`; one card's task updates do not change another card's bar.
+* Existing Run button states, popup opening, schedule marker, and card footer controls keep current behavior.
+* Progress bar exposes determinate value and completed/total context to assistive technology, works in light and dark themes, and focused tests plus app lint pass.
